title: Implicit Returns

docs.title: Functions — Functions With an Implicit Return

hints: A function whose body is a single expression doesn't need `return` — and `switch` can be that expression.
Switch on `n` with a one-sided range `..<0`, the value `0`, and `default`.
jsBridge: Like JS arrow functions `x => x * 2`, Swift single-expression bodies return implicitly. Since Swift 5.9 that includes `switch` and `if` **expressions**, which JS arrows can't contain without braces.

compass.q: An arrow function with braces needs `return`. What's the Swift rule: when exactly may `return` be omitted?
Add a `print` inside one `switch` branch. Does implicit return still work?
SwiftUI `body` relies on implicit return plus result builders. Why does adding a `let` inside `body` sometimes still work?
`switch` expression vs a dictionary lookup `[-1: "negative", …]`: which is exhaustive?
